requirements.fact: Golf carts lack rubber enclosed insulation and offer zero protection against direct lightning strikes.
requirements.misconception: Golf carts provide complete protection from lightning strikes during sudden thunderstorms on open fairways.
pamphlet_excerpts: Lightning Evacuation Protocol: Sirens mandate instant clearing of fairways to reach designated grounded lightning storm shelters.
Heat Exhaustion Response: Move overheated players into shaded areas while loosening garments and providing cool water.
Blister Prevention Strategy: Friction on walking heels requires prompt application of adhesive moleskin patches before irritation.
Severe Weather Stance: Avoid isolated tall trees and metal flagsticks during rapid thunderstorm development on fairways.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Golfers must immediately clear open fairways and seek grounded lightning shelters upon hearing severe weather detection sirens. Treatment for heat illness or ankle sprains requires immediate shade, hydration, and elevation before resuming play.
requirements.safety_callout: Clear the course immediately when thunder sounds or lightning detection sirens activate, never seeking shelter under isolated trees.
socratic_questions: Why does holding a graphite or steel golf club during an incoming storm drastically heighten strike risks?
How do early symptoms of dehydration impair a golfer's physical balance and shot execution?
What immediate steps should your group take if a stray golf ball strikes an adjacent player?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Sound Assessment: Check local course weather sirens and scan horizon clouds before teeing off.
Step 2 - Shelter Relocation: Evacuate exposed hilltops immediately and enter fully enclosed clubhouses or maintenance sheds.
Step 3 - Equipment Grounding: Drop metal clubs and golf bags far away from your direct location.
Step 4 - Physical First Aid: Administer water and apply cold packs to soothe acute golfer heat cramps.

requirements.fact: Breaching etiquette standards can result in disqualification or stroke penalties under official governing rules.
requirements.misconception: Golf etiquette rules are optional informal recommendations that carry no competitive penalty points.
pamphlet_excerpts: Governance Authority Alignment: Official competition standards derive from either the USGA rulebook or PDGA regulations.
Player Consideration Codes: Courtesy rules mandate absolute silence and stationary stance while fellow competitors address lies.
Pace of Play Standards: Groups must maintain position with the preceding group to prevent severe fairway congestion.
Course Care Responsibilities: Repairing fairway divots and pitch marks preserves turf health for upcoming tournament rounds.
requirements.pamphlet_summary: Players select either traditional golf or disc golf to master sport-specific governance bodies and conduct codes. Both disciplines emphasize safety margins, player consideration, and strict adherence to defined ball or disc lies.
requirements.safety_callout: Never swing a club or throw a disc until all players and course workers stand safely clear ahead.
socratic_questions: How do the core principles of etiquette protect player safety on active courses?
Why must a competitor play the ball or disc precisely as it lies in hazards?
What effect does slow play have on course rhythm and tournament scheduling integrity?
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Option Selection: Choose between traditional ball golf and disc golf based on local facilities.
Step 2 - Rulebook Consultation: Read defined competition rules regarding out of bounds markers and hazard penalties.
Step 3 - Etiquette Demonstration: Practice quiet standing positions behind players during their swings or disc throws.
Step 4 - Scorecard Tracking: Record individual gross strokes and penalty infractions accurately across every completed hole.

sub_requirements.fact: While loose impediments can be touched under modern rules, moving the ball causes a one stroke penalty.
sub_requirements.misconception: Golfers may freely move natural loose impediments located inside penalty areas without penalty strokes.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: The USGA Rules of Golf establish formal procedures for order of play, stroke penalties, and putting green standards. Golfers maintain course integrity by raking bunkers, replacing divots, and repairing green ball marks.

sub_requirements.fact: PDGA courtesy rule 812 mandates checking blind landing zones before releasing discs to prevent injuries.
sub_requirements.misconception: Disc golfers can throw toward blind baskets without checking walking paths for park visitors.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: The PDGA Official Rules outline courtesy guidelines including distraction avoidance, prompt throwing times, and target clearing. Players must keep public park walkways clear and avoid throwing when park visitors walk within range.
